map.Lessons 5-4 & 5-5 — compound area and th: Lessons 5-4 & 5-5: compound area and the volume of rectangular prisms (fractional edges included). Three reader gates come before the concrete sets.
map.Previously: the floor plans were drawn,: Last time: the floor plans were drawn. Hargrove's one-base trapezoid was exposed in front of the whole council.
map.Previously, in Episode 1: the crew's dra: Last time, in Episode 1: the crew's drawings beat Hargrove's. Now the cement truck is booked for Friday, and the forms have to be RIGHT.
map.I'll just… independently verify your mea: I'll just… check your measurements myself. With my own tape. Just so you know.
The patio's not a rectangle, it's an L. No single formula fits, so we SPLIT it into shapes that have formulas.
map.Compound figures get decomposed: cut the: Compound figures get decomposed: cut them into rectangles and triangles. Find each area. Then add them up.
map.Decomposition protocol: area survives cu: Decomposition rule: area stays the same when you cut. The L's total is exactly the sum of its parts. No more, no less.
map.Reader — total the patio before Fenwick: Reader, find the patio's total before Fenwick "checks" it wrong!
map.The L-shaped patio decomposes into a 8 m: The L-shaped patio decomposes into a 8 m × 5 m rectangle and a 4 m × 3 m rectangle. What is the TOTAL area to pour?
map.Conceptual: area survives cutting — find: Conceptual: area stays the same when you cut. Find each rectangle's area, then add the two together.
map.Procedural: big piece 8 × 5. Small piece: Procedural: big piece 8 × 5. Small piece 4 × 3. Then add the two products, not the side lengths.
map.Soil order time. Volume is length × widt: Soil order time. Volume is length × width × height: three dimensions, one chain of multiplying.
map.Fractional edges are not optional decima: Decimal edges count too. 2.5 metres of depth means every cubic metre counts, even the half-layers.
map.Volume of a rectangular prism = length ×: Volume of a rectangular prism = length × width × height. It works the same when an edge is a fraction or decimal.
map.Conceptual: volume fills three direction: Conceptual: volume fills three directions, so multiply all three edges. A 2.5 means the half-layer of cubes counts too.
map.Thursday. Fenwick posts his \"independen: Thursday. Fenwick puts up his own "check" on the fence.
map.The plans say HALF a metre deep. He just: The plans say HALF a metre deep. With one fake digit, he doubled the city's concrete bill.
map.One wrong dimension doesn't add a little: One wrong dimension doesn't add a little error. It MULTIPLIES the whole answer.
map.The stage deck: a 10-by-6 rectangle plus: The stage deck: a 10-by-6 rectangle plus a triangle wing. A compound shape, so Episode 1 rules apply.
map.Friday's pour needs BOTH numbers: the de: Friday's pour needs BOTH numbers: the deck's area in square metres and the slab's volume in cubic metres. Then we check Fenwick.
map.Truck's here! Reader — run the final num: Truck's here! Reader, run the final numbers while I hold the chute!
map.Boss Gate: the deck's compound area, the: Boss Gate: the deck's compound area, the slab's true volume, and the mistake in Fenwick's 24.
map.BOSS GATE. Three locks. The concrete is: BOSS GATE. Three locks. The concrete is starting to set. No pressure. (Okay, some pressure.)
map.The truck is running. Three locks: the s: The truck is running. Three locks. The stage deck is a 10 m × 6 m rectangle plus a triangle (base 6 m, height 4 m). The slab below it is 6 m × 4 m × 0.5 m. Fenwick billed the slab at 24 m³.
map.Conceptual: the deck is compound — recta: Conceptual: the deck is compound, so add the rectangle's area and the triangle's area. The slab is a prism, so multiply three edges. 0.5 is one of them.
map.Procedural: Lock 1: (10 × 6) + (6 × 4 ÷: Procedural: Lock 1: (10 × 6) + (6 × 4 ÷ 2). Lock 2: 6 × 4 × 0.5. Lock 3: compare Fenwick's 24 to your Lock 2. What did he change?
map.Twelve cubic metres ordered, twelve pour: Twelve cubic metres ordered, twelve poured, none wasted. The city refused Fenwick's bill.
map.Next week: paint and canvas. Everything: Next week: paint and canvas. Everything we built has to get WRAPPED, and wrapping is surface area.
map.Compound area.Cut the shape into pieces: Compound area.Cut the shape into pieces that have formulas, then add: the L-patio = (8×5) + (4×3) = 52 m².
map.Volume.Length × width × height — and a 2: Volume.Length × width × height. A 2.5 m edge means the halves count: 4 × 3 × 2.5 = 30 m³.
map.Audit habit.One faked dimension multipli: Audit habit.One fake dimension multiplies the whole bill. Check every factor.
map.completed Unit 5 · Episode 2: Solid Grou: finished Unit 5 · Episode 2: Solid Ground and showed mastery of compound area and the volume of rectangular prisms.
map.A different L: a 6 × 4 rectangle joined: A new L: a 6 × 4 rectangle joined to a 3 × 2 rectangle.
map.Your turn — same idea, different numbers: Your turn. Same idea, new numbers:
map.Times the height: 6 × 1.5 = 9 cubic metr: Next, times the height: 6 × 1.5 = 9 cubic metres. The .5 adds a half-layer: 6 + 3 = 9.
map.A different deck: 8 × 5 rectangle plus a: A new deck: 8 × 5 rectangle plus a triangle with base 4, height 3.
map.Its slab 5 × 4 × 0.5 = 10 m³ — half a me: Its slab 5 × 4 × 0.5 = 10 m³. Half a metre of depth means HALF of 5 × 4.
map.That's only the BIG rectangle. The L has: That is only the BIG rectangle. The L has a second piece. Add it.
map.You added side lengths. Area multiplies: You added side lengths. Multiply first: each rectangle is length × width. THEN add.
map.You dropped the half metre! 2.5, not 2 —: You dropped the half metre! It is 2.5, not 2. The half-layer is real soil.
map.You ADDED the edges. Volume multiplies:: You ADDED the edges. For volume, multiply all three dimensions.
map.Lock 3 holds. Compare 24 to your Lock 2: Lock 3 holds. Compare 24 to your Lock 2 answer. It is exactly DOUBLE. Which dimension doubles it?
map.ALL LOCKS OPEN. 72 m² of deck, 12 m³ of: ALL LOCKS OPEN. 72 m² of deck, 12 m³ of slab, and Fenwick's doubled depth caught before the bill was paid. SOLID GROUND.
